Etali

A bilingual web application, written for a basic Android phone, that carries a small business from its first offer to a decision backed by its own figures: a public storefront, a unified inbox, quotes and invoices with deposits and partial payments, a money view that separates invoiced, collected and spent, a six-month decision simulator and an assistant, Kola, that only drafts. Twenty guided demonstrations, a 25-volume academy and two books (313 and 185 printed pages) teach the method; plans are paid through a person on WhatsApp, by Mobile Money or in kind.

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed and built the whole product: information architecture, the domain engines, the local-first store, twenty guided demonstrations, the content and PDF pipeline, the two books and the payment model. The hard part was making every flow demonstrable on a phone without collecting real personal or payment data, while keeping a clean seam for the server.

A tailor opens a request pasted from WhatsApp. The page is a client island hydrated over the same seeded snapshot the server rendered; reading goes through useSyncExternalStore, and accepting Kola's draft quote calls mutate(), which clones the document, applies the change, appends an audit entry and persists the new version. Totals, deposit and balance come from the pure documents engine, which the unit tests exercise directly. Only an optional model call or a provider checkout leaves the device, through a server route.

Key engineering decisions

01

Local-first before the server

Every flow works in the browser with fictional data, so the product can be shown and tested without collecting personal data before data-protection registration. All writes go through one mutate() function, which is exactly where the server API will be plugged in.

02

Deterministic engines before a language model

Quotes, money, the simulator and Kola work offline, cost nothing per request and show their assumptions. A model is an upgrade behind a key, never a dependency, and nothing is sent without approval.

03

Payment as people already pay

No card and no automatic debit: plans by the week, month or year, settled with a person on WhatsApp, by Mobile Money or in kind. Etali never holds funds; licensed providers do, which avoids an escrow licence.

04

Books measured on the real PDF

Page counts come from the printed file, not from a word estimate, and the print step reports any element wider than the page, because a single wide table made Chrome shrink a whole book.

Notes for reviewers

Data modelA single versioned document (users, businesses, listings, customers, inquiries, quotes, invoices, payments, expenses, jobs, bookings, posts, approvals, audit) seeded from a fixed date so server and client agree; bumping the version reseeds every device.
SecurityPayment adapters are server-only and confirm status by re-querying the provider; customer text passed to the model is fenced and its output validated against allowed action types; Kola reads only what the owner permits.
TestingA demo walk signs in as each of the twenty owners and asserts the step counter and highlight on every screen; a mobile audit flags elements wider than 390 px; a stability check caught a carousel that scrolled the page back to the top.
Limits and next stepsConnect the Postgres API with phone sign-in and an offline outbox, switch on merchant keys, publish the remaining academy lessons and write the English editions of both books.
01

Problem statement

Most small enterprises in Africa keep their business in memory, in WhatsApp threads and in a notebook. Agreements are oral, deposits are rarely asked for, customer credit has no ceiling, and the owner cannot say whether a month made money. Existing tools assume a laptop, a card, steady bandwidth and English, and many products aimed at this market promise income rather than method. The design question was what a phone-first tool must do so that a tailor, a mechanic or a farmer writes before working, asks for a deposit before spending, and decides from figures, without requiring a bank card or an always-on connection.

02

Contribution

A complete operating cycle in seven screens: show (storefront with prices from or on quote, verified reviews only), receive (one inbox for form requests, pasted WhatsApp messages and noted calls), price (quotes split into labour, materials and other, with deposit and validity), collect (invoices with partial payments, polite reminders, receipts), count (invoiced, collected and spent kept apart, expenses by category), grow (customers, segments, follow-ups, a marketing calendar) and decide (Kola and a simulator). Around it: a discovery engine that proposes three realistic activities with costs and a seven-day test, twenty guided demonstrations of common trades, a 25-volume academy, two books, and a pricing page built on how people already pay, including payment in kind.

03

Architecture

Next.js 16 App Router serves every page under a locale segment; proxy.ts, the renamed middleware, resolves the language from a cookie or Accept-Language and rewrites /@handle to the storefront. Public, indexable pages (landing, storefronts, listings, lessons, legal) are server components with static parameters and JSON-LD; working screens are client islands hydrated over a deterministic snapshot generated from a fixed date, so the server render and the first client render match. State is one versioned document in localStorage, exposed through useSyncExternalStore; every write goes through a single mutate function that clones the state, applies the change and appends an audit entry, which is the seam where a Postgres API (35-model Prisma schema already written) will replace local storage. Domain logic is pure TypeScript shared by server and client. An AI route adds a model only when a key is configured, and payment adapters for CinetPay, Flutterwave and MTN MoMo verify webhooks by re-querying the provider.

04

Method and data

Each engine is deterministic and explains its numbers. Document totals, deposits, balances and state transitions are computed from line items; the simulator replays the last thirty days as a monthly baseline and projects six months for a decision (price elasticity, a hire, equipment on credit, advertising, delivery), reporting profit, cash and the orders needed to keep the gross margin; Kola is a rules engine over the owner's records that writes its assumptions next to every draft. Content follows a build pipeline: lessons and book chapters are Markdown with front matter, compiled into generated modules; book pages are measured on a real PDF printed by headless Chrome at 6 by 9 inches, and a guard reports any element wider than the printable area so the type never shrinks. Photographs and footage are real stock (Pexels licence), listed in a manifest and downloaded by a GitHub Actions job; the screens in the second book are captured from the running application by the same scripts that test the guided demos.

05

Verification and limitations

Validation is scripted: 37 unit tests on the domain engines, a 98-check end-to-end journey suite, a run that walks all twenty guided demos through their 220 steps and asserts each highlight, a phone-width audit of 36 screens for horizontal overflow, and a scroll-stability check that fails if the landing page moves by itself. Limits: data lives on the device until the server API is connected, so there is no sync between phones; payments are simulated until merchant keys are configured; Kola runs without a language model by default; the academy publishes its lessons in reviewed batches; the English editions of the books are still to be written. Etali promises no income.
